citation.title: Topology optimization of 2D structures with nonlinearities using deep learning
citation.authors: Diab W. Abueidda, Seid Koric, Nahil A. Sobh

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The CNN predicts topology optimization designs without iterative optimization and with negligible inference time compared with the optimization framework used for its training designs.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No numeric inference time or matched speed-up is reported; Section 3.1 gives classical run times only.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion says laptop inference is effectively immediate versus expensive nonlinear optimization; Section 3.1 gives 25 and 90 minute classical laptop times.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP topology optimization using sensitivity-based MMA (Section 2.1)
baseline.implementation: ABAQUS/TOSCA for elasticity and hyperelasticity; in-house MATLAB for stress constraint (Sections 2.1, 3.2)
baseline.hardware_classical: iForge Intel/Skylake 40-core nodes with 192 GB RAM, up to ten jobs concurrently; laptop CORE i5 vPro for single-job comparison (Section 3.1)
baseline.hardware_ml: iForge NVIDIA v100 32 GB GPU for training; laptop for inference, specification not stated (Sections 5, 6)
baseline.problem_size: 32 x 32 elements, linear; 50 x 50 elements, hyperelastic and stress-constrained (Sections 3.1-3.2)
baseline.classical_time: roughly 25 minutes per linear task and around 90 minutes per nonlinear task on CORE i5 vPro laptop (Section 3.1)
baseline.ml_time: not stated numerically; described as negligible or instantaneous (abstract; Section 6)
baseline.training_time: 1.25 hrs linear and 1.5 hrs nonlinear on single v100; 12.5 hrs linear on CPU-only Skylake node (Section 5, Figure 7)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 15,000 linear pairs at 0.31 minutes/data point; 18,000 nonlinear pairs at 3.2 minutes/data point with ten concurrent optimizations; 20,000 stress pairs, time not stated (Sections 3.1-3.2)
baseline.quality_metric: Dice similarity coefficient and mean squared error of density images (Sections 4.2, 5)
baseline.quality_gap: test mean DSC 0.958 linear, 0.964 hyperelastic, 0.984 stress constrained versus classical designs (Section 5, Figures 10-13)

R1.evidence: Abstract and Section 5: inference speed is claimed, while comparison to optimizer outputs uses image similarity; no matched FE objective or wall-clock budget is shown.

R2.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 3.1: baseline uses ABAQUS/TOSCA commercial optimization; solver efficiency is not characterized and no direct strong-baseline comparison is given.

R3.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 5: data-generation rates and GPU training hours are stated, but no break-even uses or total cost accounting is given.

R4.evidence: Section 5, Figures 10-13: test quality is assessed by density-image DSC and selected visual examples, without FE evaluation of returned designs or failure-rate accounting.

reporting.n_test_cases: 1,500 linear, 1,800 nonlinear, 2,000 stress-constrained [inferred from 10% test split and dataset sizes, Sections 3.1-3.2 and 5]

notes: The supplied full text does not give a numeric inference timing; the reported GPU-versus-CPU training comparison is not the primary classical TO comparison.
